gnash.e: From Middle English gnasten. Origin unknown; the word is probably either Germanic or ultimately onomatopoeic.
gnash.g: To grind (one's teeth) in pain or in anger.

gnat.e: From Middle English gnat, from Old English gnætt (“gnat; midge; mosquito”), from Proto-West Germanic *gnatt, *gnattu, from Proto-Germanic *gnattaz, *gnattuz (“gnat”), from Proto-Indo-European *gʰneHdʰn-, *gʰneHd- (“to gnaw; scratch”), from Proto-Indo-European *gʰen- (“to gnaw; bite; scratch; grind”). Related also gnit and gnaw.
gnat.g: A biting insect, especially a mosquito.

gnaw.e: From Middle English gnawen, gnaȝen, from Old English gnagan, from Proto-West Germanic *gnagan, from Proto-Germanic *gnaganą (“to gnaw”), probably from Proto-Indo-European *gʰnēgʰ- (“to gnaw, scratch”).
gnaw.g: To bite something persistently, especially something tough.

gnawing.e: From Middle English gnawynge; equivalent to gnaw + -ing.
